newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia confident of 97 sugar quotas despite delays.
newsitem.headline: Russia confident of 97 sugar quotas despite delays.

text.p: Russia is confident that its delayed plan to slap quotas on refined sugar imports will become reality this year, despite opposition to the proposal, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha said on Friday.
"There are some forces which are trying to oppose this plan, but we will resolve this problem," he told a news conference.
"We should restrict the arbitrary import of this product (white sugar)."
Russia plans to restrict white sugar imports to 1.5 million tonnes a year to shore up struggling domestic sugar refineries.
Out of that total, imports from Ukraine would be capped at 1.15 million tonnes.
Zaveryukha would not say when the curbs would be introduced.
A Foreign Trade Ministry order in August 1996 called for the protectionist measures, but the government has so far failed to act, casting doubts over whether the curbs will be implemented.
Domestic sugar plants want to process Cuban raws rather than face competition from Ukrainian and European refined supplies.
Zaveryukha said Ukrainian refiners had an unfair advantage over Russian ones and the latter needed protection.
"How can our producers work when producers in Ukraine are working without having to pay value-added tax, a tax which our producers have to work with?" he said.

Interfax news agency quoted Alexander Rubinchik, vice-president of big Russian comodities trader Menatep-Impex, as saying the absence of limits on white sugar imports was ruinous for the domestic sugar industry.
But Rubinchik was quoted as saying that options beyond simple quotas were under consideration, including regulatory tariffs.
